question: On interchanging signs + and ÷, and numbers 7 and 9, which of the following equations would be correct?
solution: **Explanation:** BODMAS Rule: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab9003ba65914e9db049e6f510b5740718252ca1bdf98a9ac303e65c8cd29d3e.png] Interchanging the signs and numbers we get, First we will check options as: 1) 7 + 3 – 4 ÷ 9 × 5 = 40 Applying the changes we will get, ⇒ 9 ÷ 3 - 4 + 7 × 5 = 40 Using the BODMAS rule, we will get, ⇒ __9 ÷ 3__ - 4 + 7 × 5 = 40 ⇒ 3 - 4 + __**7 × 5**__ = 40 ⇒ __**3 - 4 + 35**__ = 40 ⇒ 34 = 40, is not possible 2) 7 × 3 + 3 ÷ 9 - 5 = 12 Applying the changes we will get,
